title: Conditions of Claim Intake — Travel Protection Plans
content:
A claim on a Travel Protection Plans certificate is filed against one named benefit for one incident, and a single incident that touches two benefits is filed as two claims.

## Conditions that must hold at intake

**The incident date.** The traveller states in this conversation the date on which the incident they are claiming for occurred. That date comes from the traveller's own statement, and it is recorded against the claim reference the claim is filed under.

**The standing of the certificate.** A claim is filed only while the policy record stands in force or expired. Those two are the whole of what the record may show for a claim to be filed; the certificate's own status is what decides it, not what the traveller believes the certificate to be.

**The filing and document deadlines.** A claim must be filed within the plan's filing deadline counted from the incident, and supporting documents must reach the insurer within the plan's document deadline counted from filing. A claim filed late is declined for lateness alone.

**Delay triggers.** A baggage delay claim is payable only from the plan's delay trigger onward, a travel delay claim only from its delay trigger onward, and a missed connection claim only from its own trigger. A delay short of the trigger gives rise to no claim at all.

**Cancellation for any reason.** Such a claim is filed only on a plan that includes it, only where notice was given at least the plan's notice hours before departure, and only where the trip was cancelled outright rather than changed.

## A clause no longer in force

The condition that "A claim is filed only when no claim carrying the same claim reference has already been filed on this policy." is **no longer in force** on Travel Protection Plans certificates; what stops a second claim being opened is settled on the current basis for claim intake and not by this standard. Every other condition set out above stands as a condition in force, and the plan figures this standard reads — the filing deadlines, the document deadlines, the three delay triggers and the notice hours — are valid as scheduled.

## Counting claims in a term

The claims filed on a certificate in a term are counted over the whole policy term, from the issue date to the expiry or cancellation date, as the number of claims filed on that certificate.

## Two intake readings

A traveller whose baggage arrived 9 hours late, on a plan whose baggage delay benefit is payable from 12 hours, has no claim under that benefit at all, because the delay is short of the trigger. Had the baggage arrived 12 hours late, the benefit would be payable from that point.

A traveller whose one incident damaged baggage and also cut the journey short files two claims, one against the baggage benefit and one against the interruption benefit, because a claim is filed against one named benefit for one incident.

superseded_clauses: A claim is filed only when no claim carrying the same claim reference has already been filed on this policy.
